title: Speak-No-Evil Monkey Emoji 🙊 Meaning: Oops and Secrets
description: The speak-no-evil monkey emoji 🙊 covers its mouth. It means 'oops, I said too much,' keeping a secret, or stifling a giggle. Examples, combos and FAQs.
summary: The 🙊 speak-no-evil monkey emoji shows a monkey with both hands over its mouth. It means the sender said something they should not have, is holding back a secret, or is trying not to laugh. The tone is cheeky and playful, a visual 'oops' or 'my lips are sealed.'
meaning: Clapping a hand over your mouth is the universal sign of a slip. 🙊 follows spilled gossip, a blunt opinion, an accidental swear word, or a spoiler that got out. It works as a mock apology: the sender is not truly sorry, and the wide eyes show they know exactly what they said. That makes it a favorite for delivering a spicy remark and softening it in the same breath.

It is equally good for secrets still being kept. 'I know what you're getting for your birthday 🙊' teases without telling. People use it to promise discretion, to hint that they have news they cannot share yet, and to react when someone else reveals something juicy. In flirting it marks a daring line, similar to the eye-covering monkey but with the stress on what was said instead of on shyness.

The image comes from the three wise monkeys of Japanese tradition, carved most famously at the Toshogu shrine in Nikko, where this figure is named Iwazaru. The proverb's point, to refrain from speaking evil, survives when the emoji is used for biting your tongue, declining to comment, or staying silent about wrongdoing. That last sense can be critical, pointing at people who keep quiet when they should speak up.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It closes a message that went a bit far: 'honestly her ex was better 🙊.' It also covers surprises and confidences. Friends use it to signal that information is not to be repeated. A solo 🙊 in reply to gossip means 'I can't believe you said that, tell me more.'

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: After a flirtatious or suggestive comment, 🙊 plays innocent. It lets the sender test a bolder line while pretending it slipped out. If someone sends it after admitting they think you are cute, they are being coy and hoping you will respond in kind.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Creators use it for teasers and unannounced projects, hinting that news is coming. It tags hot takes and 'unpopular opinion' posts. In comments, it reacts to shade and savage replies, standing for a gasp behind the hand or a laugh the commenter is trying to hold in.

examples.text: I accidentally told Dad about the surprise party 🙊
examples.meaning: Admitting to letting a secret slip.

examples.text: Big news coming Friday but I can't say yet 🙊
examples.meaning: Teasing an announcement while staying quiet.
A cheeky criticism with a pretend-guilty tone.
Flirtatious embarrassment at being caught looking.

examples.text: Not saying a word about what I saw last night 🙊
examples.meaning: Promising, playfully, to keep something confidential.

examples.text: Trying not to laugh in this meeting 🙊
examples.meaning: Stifling a giggle at an inappropriate moment.

combos.meaning: See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil: staying out of it.
A secret that must not be repeated.
Laughing at something you probably should not have said.
Gossip, or 'tea,' that the sender is reluctantly spilling.

confusedWith.difference: 🤭 is a yellow face giggling behind one hand, used for coy laughter or polite shock. 🙊 covers the whole mouth with both hands and leans more toward 'oops' and secrecy. The monkey is the cheekier of the two.
🙈 hides its eyes out of shyness or cringe. 🙊 hides its mouth because of something said or unsaid. Use the eyes for embarrassment about being seen and the mouth for regrets about speaking.
🤐 shows a mouth zipped shut and means a firm promise of silence or being forbidden to speak. 🙊 is lighter and often used after the secret is already out.

avoid: Do not add it to a truly hurtful comment as cover, because 'oops' does not undo an insult.
Avoid it when discussing confidential work matters, where hinting at secrets looks indiscreet.
Never use monkey emojis to refer to a person's race; that is a racist use.
design: A brown monkey's face seen head-on, with both hands placed over its mouth and round, wide eyes above them. Most platforms give it a lighter face and ears against darker fur. The amount of face hidden by the hands and the precise eye expression vary slightly, but the gesture is identical everywhere.

faqs.q: What does 🙊 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She said something bold, cheeky, or revealing and is playing it off, or she is keeping a secret. In flirting it often follows a compliment or a suggestive joke. It signals playfulness, not real regret.

faqs.q: What does 🙊 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: He let something slip or is teasing that he knows more than he is saying. If it follows a flirty remark, he is checking your reaction while keeping things light.
Both cover the mouth. 🤭 suggests a giggle or mild surprise and looks demure. 🙊 suggests a blurted remark or a guarded secret and feels more mischievous.
Yes, that is one of its main uses. It can mean 'I won't tell,' 'I can't tell yet,' or 'I just told and shouldn't have.' The surrounding words show which.
